narrative: Inventory optimization analysis for material PL1__ME953731 reveals a smooth demand pattern with a coefficient of variation of 13.02%. The demand exhibits a left-skewed distribution with mean daily demand of 2,138 units and a statistically significant downward trend. Lead time analysis shows unstable performance (CV=65.03%) with mean lead time of 1.30 days and standard deviation of 0.85 days. The optimized (r,Q) policy recommends a safety stock of 3,020 units, a reorder point of 7,609 units, and an order quantity of 13,432 units, achieving the 95% service level target while reducing total annual inventory costs by $3,694.89 (42.1%). The recommended safety lead time of 1.41 days is lower than the current SAP setting of 3.0 days.

research_insights.selected_model: EOQ with stochastic lead time demand — continuous-review (r,Q) policy
research_insights.selection_rationale: Selected due to smooth demand pattern (CV=13.02%) and unstable lead time (CV=65%). The model accounts for both demand and lead time variability using the combined-variance safety stock formula: SS = z * sqrt(LT*σ_D² + D²*σ_LT²). Continuous review is appropriate given the high daily volume and cost sensitivity.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Lead time instability (CV=65%) is the dominant risk driver, contributing ~50% of total variance through transport uncertainty. Close monitoring and supplier SLA enforcement are essential to sustain the 95% service level.
